about: Byte caps on the tools/list result (compact JSON, as the stdio shim writes it) per schema profile, protocol version and role profile. Measured 2026-09-25 (WS-54); remember content made optional and the WS-19A lifecycle arguments added as Advanced 2026-09-26, and the WS-19B provenance and evidence-bound vote arguments the same day, and the WS-20 recall filters, disclosure and budget arguments and remember's kind, topic and tags the same day (full caps grew by exactly their cost each time; the WS-20 argument descriptions live at xmustard://docs/tools, not in the schema). WS-18 (2026-09-28): the search description now names BM25 over bodies and lost 59 bytes, search's outputSchema gained omitted and next_cursor (58 bytes, 2025-06-18 only), and the Advanced cursor and path_glob arguments cost 198 bytes in the full profile; lean caps were lowered to the measured sizes. WS-21 (2026-09-28): why_failed run_id became optional and the tool non-read-only (command mode runs commands); its lean entry shrank by 9 bytes at 2025-06-18 (command, off by default, left the description) and by 53 bytes at 2024-11-05 (caps lowered), and the full caps grew by exactly the cost of its five advanced source arguments (621 bytes at 2025-06-18, 577 at 2024-11-05). WS-20 review round 2 (2026-09-28): recall's Advanced session_id gained maxLength 128, 16 bytes in the full profile only. WS-35 (2026-09-28): impact's description now names the resolved Go/TS graph and its completeness (32 bytes shorter), max_depth allows 32 with a shorter description, and its outputSchema lists by_depth for impacted and risk (25 bytes, 2025-06-18 only): lean caps were lowered by the measured 18 bytes (2025-06-18) and 43 (2024-11-05). impact's twelve Advanced v2 arguments (direction, relation_types, min_confidence, include_tests, limit, offset, summary_only, timeout_ms, scope, base, head, worktree) cost the full profile 1,292 bytes at 2025-06-18 and 1,292 at 2024-11-05 over the lowered lean sizes; the full caps grew by exactly that (+1,274 and +1,249 over their old caps). WS-27 (2026-09-28): the recall description names the conflict tiers in 3 fewer bytes (lean caps lowered), and the full caps grew by exactly the cost of recall's Advanced include_merged, subject and predicate (161 bytes) and remember's Advanced claims and relations (125 bytes), described at xmustard://docs/tools. Lower a cap when the list shrinks; never raise one to fit an addition: advertise less (declare the argument Advanced, documented at xmustard://docs/tools) or trim a description. cmd/xmustard-api checks role_profiles against the route gates. WS-FIX-05 (2026-09-28): impact gained path= (file-level blast radius), listed in the lean schema by owner decision; every cap rose by exactly its measured 119 bytes (the path property 79, the description's path= clause 34, max_depth's description naming path= 6), for every profile, role and protocol version. WS-35 merged with WS-FIX-05 (2026-09-28): path= keeps its lean property, the description's clause became "path= → a file's lexical referrers" and max_depth's description "hops (default 3; path= 4)", and the caps are the measured sizes, 116 bytes above WS-35's lowered caps and below WS-FIX-05's (lean) in every profile, role and version. WS-33 merged with WS-35 (2026-09-28): ground's Advanced session_id and its new sections value session, and remember's Advanced session_id (handoff capsules), 64 bytes each in the full profile only (reader and verifier +64, proposer and agent +128 over WS-35's full caps); lean caps unchanged. WS-27 merged after WS-35 and WS-FIX-05 (2026-09-28), independently of WS-33 (lean -3 everywhere; full +158 reader and verifier, +283 proposer and agent over the WS-35+WS-FIX-05 base). WS-33 merged with WS-27 (this branch, 2026-09-29): both deltas are additive over the same WS-35+WS-FIX-05 base (WS-33 touches ground and remember's session_id; WS-27 touches recall and remember's claims/relations), so the full caps are the sum of both deltas over that base; lean caps take WS-27's lowered values (WS-33 left lean unchanged). These were sums worked out by hand from each side's stated delta, never measured; WS-HYG-01 re-measured them. WS-36 (2026-09-28): search gained mode=symbol (an enum value, its mode description, and a description clause that replaced pattern mode's example, 4 bytes shorter) and explain's path stopped being required (explain also takes symbol= and uid=); together every lean cap fell by 5 bytes, and the full caps grew by exactly the 1,349 bytes of the new Advanced arguments over the lowered lean sizes (search max_chars, kinds, depth, include_body, include_info, substring; explain symbol, uid, depth, chain_depth, include_content, max_chars, limit, cursor; impact max_chars). WS-36 merged with WS-33 (2026-09-29): both deltas are additive, so the full caps are WS-36's plus WS-33's session_id cost (reader and verifier +64, proposer and agent +128); lean caps are WS-36's. WS-31 merged with WS-33 (2026-09-29): the Advanced ground since_revision argument (200 bytes) and remember tier (124 bytes, remember-capable profiles) were added on top of session_id; full caps rose by exactly that. WS-28 (2026-09-30): recall's Advanced as_of, valid_only and seed (167 bytes, described at xmustard://docs/tools); lean caps unchanged, every full cap rose by exactly that. WS-HYG-01 (2026-10-02) re-measured every cap with TestToolsListStaysWithinByteCaps on the Linux build box and set each one to the measured size: the full caps fell by 156 bytes (reader, verifier) and 241 bytes (proposer, agent) in both protocol versions, and the lean caps were already at their measured sizes, so they did not change. All caps below are the measured sizes; a future addition re-measures rather than summing deltas. WS-59b (2026-10-02): search gained mode=text (an enum member, its description clause, and lang's second meaning as a language filter) with no new argument, so the additions were paid for by advertising less inside search: its description, mode's, lang's, q's and seed's descriptions and the Advanced substring's were each shortened (search's own description keeps the phrases 'function bodies' and 'doc sections', which descriptions_test.go pins and which say what the lane reads: shortening them to 'bodies' and 'docs' makes a code body indistinguishable from a doc comment), and every full cap the trimmed list came under was lowered by its measured byte, 1 byte each for all four 2025-06-18 role profiles and for proposer, verifier, agent and reader at 2024-11-05. Review round 2 (2026-10-02): lang gained maxLength 256, the same bound as path_glob and the bound the route enforces, so a schema-valid lang is no longer refused at the route. The 14 lean and 9 full bytes it costs were paid for inside search by shortening mode's and seed's descriptions; every cap is unchanged from the values above. No cap rose. WS-59e (2026-10-03): impact's tier paging reports has_more and next_cursor in its outputSchema (62 bytes at 2025-06-18 only), and its Advanced cursor argument is declared on the tool rather than coming from budgetArgs, which omits it for a non-Paged budget tool (99 bytes in the full profile). The additions were paid for by advertising less inside impact: its description dropped the '(name, Container.name, UID, path)' clause that the symbol argument's own description now carries, and the from, to, symbol, relation_types, scope, worktree, offset, summary_only, base and head descriptions were shortened. Every cap was re-measured with TestToolsListStaysWithinByteCaps on the Linux build box and lowered to the measurement: the lean caps fell by 76 (2024-11-05) and 14 (2025-06-18), the full caps by 64 (2024-11-05) and 2 (2025-06-18), each for all four role profiles. No cap rose. WS-32a (2026-10-04): remember's Advanced job_id and decision arguments, and remember's op enum gained the job value, cost 151 bytes in every full profile and nothing in the lean profile (both arguments are Advanced, absent from the lean schema). This tree also carries WS-59e, whose description trims are not additive with these arguments, so every cap below is this merged tree's own re-measurement with TestToolsListStaysWithinByteCaps on the Linux build box, not a sum of the two deltas. No cap rose.
